articles.author: Arvid Andersson
articles.description:
Most RAG projects start vector-first: embed the documents, store them, retrieve by similarity. It works in the demo. Then a user searches for an exact thing, a product code, an error number, a specific name, and the system misses it, because vector search ranks by meaning, not by literal tokens. This post is about that failure and the retrieval architectures that fix it, as of June 2026.
An embedding turns text into a point in a space where nearby points mean similar things. That is exactly what you want for "find documents about return policies" and exactly what you do not want for "find SKU-4471". The model encodes "SKU-4471" as something close to other codes that look and read like it, so the literal one a user typed can sit just outside the top results. The same happens with error code…
articles.title: RAG Retrieval Architectures: When Better Embeddings Stop Helping

The hype cycle for AI applications has shifted. The question is no longer "can we call an API?" — it's "how do we build AI systems that are private, reliable, and cheap at scale?" Local-first AI architecture answers all three by pushing computation to the edge while keeping cloud APIs as backup, not dependency.
This is a deep-dive into the three pillars that make local-first AI production-ready: MCP (Model Context Protocol) integration for structured tool access, offline memory for persistent context without a server round-trip, and cost optimization through hybrid model routing. I'm Mahajan Ashok — AI Product Engineer, freelance full-stack dev, based out of Hyderabad. Fresh B.Tech CSE (Data Science) grad from TKR College, currently running my own freelance thing, Mahajan IT Solution, while job hunting on the side.
Quick backstory
Last year or so I've been building real stuff for real clients — not tutorials, actual production systems. Honestly what I keep gravitating toward is AI that does things, not just chats — agents wired into real tools and real data, actually moving work forward.
Why Cohort 3
"Accelerate AI with Cloud Run" is exactly my kind of learning — build-first, not another set of disconnected tutorials. One coffee shop, three labs, growing the whole time: personalized customer experience → location intelligence for expansion → automating ops to run leaner. All shipped on Cloud Run with Gemini, ADK, multi-agent orchestration.
That's basically how I work with freelance clients too — ship an MVP, layer in the intelligence, then optimize once it's actually running. Getting to do that on Google Cloud's AI-native stack, and learn how production multi-agent systems are actually supposed to be deployed, is exactly where I want to level up next.
What I'm here for
Let's build.
